X.note: The wall texture and light are strong and look like a render. The figures are stiff, smooth mannequins with blank faces and tall bicorne/shako-like hats. They march in a column, and the blue-coated men have bare white legs. The long dark cast shadow on the ground looks odd. The cannonball pile and barrels read as black blobs. The Union flag has the wrong proportions for 1782, and a flag-pole at the harbour end is plausible but too clean.

Y.note: The setting is the same and the crowd is denser and more varied, with a brown civilian and tricorne-like hats that fit 1782 better, plus a ship visible in the bay. The figures are still stiff, dollish game-asset mannequins with thin legs. The crowd overlaps and clumps, and the barrel on the left has a red-coat texture glitch, a figure fused into it. The Union flag is the 1801 or modern-looking version with the wrong proportions, and the glowing windows are the same in both frames.

why: Y has a more believable mixed crowd, tricorne-style hats, civilians and a ship in the bay, which fits a besieged 1782 town better, although it is more cluttered and has a texture glitch at the barrel.
top_fix_for_weaker: Replace the identical mannequin soldiers in X with varied tricorne-wearing figures and civilians in different poses and sizes. Remove the white bare-leg look and the black blob shadows, add ground contact shadows, and add a ship or smoke in the bay.
anachronisms_seen: Union Jack with the post-1801 or modern look; a 1782 flag would be the plain 1606 Union without the Irish saltire, and this one looks wrong in proportion
Bicorne/shako-like hats in X are not typical of 1782 infantry, which wore tricornes or cut-down round hats
Blue-coated figures with bare white legs look wrong for the period
Uniformly plastered, intact 18th-century terrace buildings in the middle of a siege, with little bombardment damage
